name: Evernote
price: Free download, core value gated behind subscription (free tier capped at ~50 notes / 1 device; Personal ~$130+/yr after repeated price hikes up to ~2x)
complaints: Price increases described as up to ~1000% over original plans; UK users cite £79.99 -> £154.90 jump after Bending Spoons acquisition
v10 Electron rewrite tanked Play reviews to waves of 1-star ('they've been 1 star ever since v10 was released' — official Evernote forum thread)
Buggy/slow/clunky app, sync failures between devices, notes not saving, repeated forced logins
Billing problems and support taking nearly a month to respond; longtime free/legacy users feel squeezed into subscription
Trustpilot 2.4/5 ('Poor'), with recent pages trending 1.6/5
freeIncumbentRisk: High: Google Keep, OneNote, Notion, Obsidian, Simplenote are free and actively developed; but the fleeing user base is actively shopping for a home, and none nail 'simple longtime-notes archive with painless import'
moatNotes: Massive install base of angry paying users with 10+ years of data; the job-to-be-done (reliable cross-device notes with local-feeling speed, one-time or cheap pricing, easy Evernote import) is well-defined; incumbents keep failing on trust, not features

name: Chrooma Keyboard - RGB & Emoji
price: Free with paid-gated premium: $2.49 one-time 'unlock all forever' IAP plus per-feature IAPs (resizing, customization)
complaints: Last updated June 3, 2020 — over 6 years abandoned while still listed and still selling lifetime-unlock IAPs
Lifetime 'Pro/Premium' buyers left with a dead app; developer (GameLounge/Loopsie SRL) pivoted to other apps
Aging codebase increasingly incompatible/buggy on modern Android versions; features paywalled then never maintained
freeIncumbentRisk: High: Gboard and SwiftKey are free and excellent; Chrooma's differentiator (app-adaptive color theming, compact one-hand modes) is cosmetic-plus-UX, which Gboard only partially copies (dynamic color arrived with Material You)
moatNotes: Proves people pay one-time for a stylish, adaptive, lightweight keyboard; a maintained privacy-respecting clone with lifetime pricing inherits 5M+ orphaned installs; keyboard switching cost is low, but trust/maintenance is the moat

name: ai.type keyboard Plus + Emoji
complaints: Last updated May 14, 2020 — paid app abandoned 6+ years while remaining purchasable
2017 breach leaked personal data of 31 million users incl. unencrypted passwords and contacts
Upstream/Secure-D caught the app generating 14M+ fraudulent premium-purchase requests from 110,000+ devices (~$18M in attempted unwanted charges)
Users speculate their typing data is still being monetized; paid buyers got neither updates nor trust remediation
freeIncumbentRisk: High: Gboard/SwiftKey free; but ai.type's paying niche wanted deep customization (layouts, long-press behaviors, themes) that Gboard refuses to offer
moatNotes: The angle is trust: 500K+ people paid $3 for a customizable keyboard whose vendor became a privacy scandal; a verifiably-offline, no-network-permission paid keyboard with ai.type-level customization directly converts this base; also inherits Swype refugees (Swype delisted 2018, users still complaining no swipe keyboard matches it)

name: Jorte Calendar & Organizer
price: Free with paid-gated Jorte Premium subscription (~$2.99/mo) plus paid icon/theme packs
complaints: Chronic 'Failed to sync' errors reported virtually daily; events silently fail to propagate to Google Calendar
Error reports and support requests go unanswered — users report never hearing back
Premium features (and even continuity across devices) tied to Jorte ID/cloud account that users distrust; paywall creep over a decade
Long-time users on forums actively asking 'any good calendar app?' to escape
freeIncumbentRisk: Very high: Google Calendar is free and default; Jorte's paying base is the 'paper-planner feel' niche (diary view, stickers, agenda aesthetics) that Google Calendar does not serve
moatNotes: 29M installs at 3.4 stars is a huge dissatisfied base; the winning clone is a planner-style calendar with rock-solid native Google Calendar sync (no proprietary cloud) and one-time pricing; still actively updated by vendor, so failure is reliability/support, not abandonment — sharpest complaint to attack is sync trust

name: Alarm Clock Plus
price: Free ad-supported with paid one-time NoAds companion app (com.vp.alarmClockPlusV2, ~$2 on Play/Amazon) — paid-gating is ad-removal, weakest of the set
ratingsCount: tens of thousands (exact count not captured; app live since May 2010)
complaints: Effectively abandoned: went ~5 years between updates; last meaningful update reported March 16, 2021
On modern Android the alarm fires but snooze/dismiss screen never appears, forcing users to power off the phone — catastrophic for an alarm app
Intermittent alarms that simply fail to go off after OS updates (Doze/background restrictions never adapted to)
Developer support email bounces — no way to get help; NoAds buyers stranded
freeIncumbentRisk: High: Google Clock is free and reliable; the paid niche is power features (dock/nightstand mode, math-to-dismiss, per-alarm volume ramp) that stock clocks skip; Alarmy owns this space now but via resented subscription (its own legacy paid app was unpublished Oct 2023)
moatNotes: Alarm apps are trust products — 'it must fire on Android 14+' is the whole pitch; a one-time-purchase, modern-API alarm with nightstand dock mode targets both Alarm Clock Plus refugees and Alarmy legacy-Pro buyers angry about the subscription pivot
